channel.title: Insights Aggregator
channel.description: Investment insights from banks & asset managers, aggregated.

item.title: The Mid-Cycle Shift Equity Investors Shouldn’t Miss
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Morgan Stanley's CIO Mike Wilson argues that equity markets are transitioning to a mid-cycle environment where leadership is shifting from capital-intensive cyclical stocks toward higher-quality, asset-light companies with durable earnings and strong free cash flow. Sectors like Software, Financial Services, Insurance, and Healthcare Services are showing earnings momentum similar to what Semiconductors displayed earlier in the year, reflecting a market confirmation of economic normalization.

item.title: Why Global Bond Yields Are Surging
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · Goldman Sachs Exchanges — Government bond yields have reached multi-decade highs globally, driven by fiscal deficits, defense spending, AI-related borrowing, resilient economic growth, and energy shocks. The persistent nature of this sell-off, despite low volatility, suggests fundamental factors rather than technical forces are at play. Multiple borrowers—governments and corporations—are competing for the same limited pool of global savings, mechanically pushing rates upward.

item.title: Must Read Research: Walmart & Ads; Quantum, Computing Power Trading; Lodging Demand
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — This research episode examines how computing power is becoming a critical economic resource, covering Walmart's expanding advertising business powered by proprietary data, the advancing timeline for quantum computing commercialization, and emerging GPU rental futures markets. The discussion also highlights strong demand trends across lodging, media, communications infrastructure, and AI-related sectors based on recent corporate conference presentations.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Societe Generale's Cross Asset Research provides analysis and insights across multiple asset classes and market themes. The platform aggregates the firm's latest publications, research reports, and video content covering global market developments and investment perspectives.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research provides investment insights and analysis across multiple asset classes and markets. The platform offers publications, research commentary, and video content covering macroeconomic trends, market conditions, and portfolio considerations for institutional and professional investors.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research team provides integrated analysis across multiple asset classes including equities, fixed income, currencies, and commodities. The research covers macro trends, market valuations, and tactical positioning to inform investment decisions across global markets.

item.title: Saudi oil supply at risk | Investing themes - CIO
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · Deutsche Bank Wealth CIO Insights (web) — Rising geopolitical tensions threaten Saudi oil supply, creating concerns about inflation and market stability. Deutsche Bank's CIO discusses the investment implications of supply disruptions and their broader impact on global markets. Investors face heightened volatility amid these interconnected macro challenges.

item.title: Inflation Redux?
item.dc:creator: AQR
item.description: AQR · AQR Research & Insights (web) — AQR analyzes inflation sensitivities and protection strategies in response to potential future inflation shocks, examining how commodities and trend-following strategies can provide hedges. The research evaluates different implementation approaches for inflation protection across portfolios.

item.title: The Macro Brief - Gold's rollercoaster ride
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Global Viewpoint — HSBC's Chief Precious Metals Analyst examines the factors driving significant gold price volatility throughout the year and discusses the potential for continued fluctuations ahead. The analysis explores the macro and market drivers behind gold's recent swings in value.

item.title: AI-conscious asset allocation: portfolio construction in a capital investment boom
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Portfolio Insights — JPMorgan's Strategic Investment Advisory Group examines how investors can capitalize on AI's potential while preserving proper portfolio diversification during a capital investment boom. The report addresses the challenge of positioning portfolios to benefit from AI adoption without taking on excessive concentration risk. The guidance aims to help investors balance growth opportunities with risk management principles.

item.title: Biotech Trends Reshaping Markets
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · MS Insights (web) — Morgan Stanley analysts identify three emerging biotech themes poised to reshape markets: artificial intelligence applications in drug development, Alzheimer's disease therapeutics, and in-vivo gene editing technologies. These developments represent major innovation trends with potential to create new commercial opportunities and transform treatment approaches across multiple therapeutic areas.

item.title: Meet the Inclusive & Sustainable Ventures 2026 Global Cohort
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · MS Insights (web) — Morgan Stanley has announced the 2026 cohort of startups and nonprofits selected for its Inclusive & Sustainable Ventures program. The initiative supports early-stage companies focused on inclusive growth and environmental sustainability across various sectors. This represents continued institutional investment in businesses aligned with ESG and impact-driven objectives.

item.title: Under the Banyan Tree - Taking the pulse on medical tourism
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Global Viewpoint — HSBC Global Research examines Asia's expanding medical tourism sector, which has evolved beyond simple healthcare trips to Thailand into a more sophisticated industry. The discussion explores the growth drivers, market dynamics, and investment opportunities within this fast-developing segment across the Asian region.

item.title: Views from the Floor Is the Bond Market Calling Washington’s Bluff?
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — Bond markets are signaling concern about sticky inflation and elevated government debt levels, creating portfolio risk through sovereign debt instruments. This dynamic suggests the bond market may be testing policymakers' ability to manage fiscal and inflation challenges. The tension between monetary policy constraints and fiscal realities is reshaping fixed-income valuations.

item.title: Why Bond Yields Are Rising and What It Means for Your Portfolio
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · BofA Private Bank Insights (web) — Bond yields have increased recently, creating mixed market signals that investors must navigate. The podcast discusses how Federal Reserve policy, inflation dynamics, and Treasury buyback programs may influence fixed income allocation decisions going forward.

item.title: Can the S&P 500 Rally as Treasury Yields Rise?
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs examines the historical relationship between rising Treasury yields, Federal Reserve rate hikes, and S&P 500 performance. While rate increases typically create near-term headwinds for equities, the analysis suggests the broad market index has historically delivered gains approximately one year after policy tightening cycles begin.

item.title: BOJ Preview: Global Market Implications
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan Global Research analysts examined the Bank of Japan's upcoming monetary policy decision and analyzed how it would affect global financial markets. The discussion covered implications across Japan's economy, currency markets, and fixed income assets, incorporating perspectives from economists and strategists.

item.title: Patients Are Taking the Driver's Seat in Healthcare
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Healthcare companies are adapting their business models as patients increasingly seek control over how they access care and purchase medicine, with growing adoption of wellness tools and wearables. Morgan Stanley analysts discuss the structural shifts in the industry driven by consumer demand for transparency and choice in healthcare decision-making.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Societe Generale's Cross Asset Research provides analysis and insights across multiple asset classes and markets. The research covers macroeconomic trends, market valuations, and interconnections between different financial instruments and regions.

item.title: US Rates: Higher for longer
item.dc:creator: Barclays
item.description: Barclays · Barclays Brief — US bond markets have repriced sharply in early 2026, with the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5% as expectations for interest rate cuts gave way to discussion of prolonged restrictive policy. Despite elevated yields and tight monetary conditions, the US economy has remained resilient, partly supported by substantial AI-related capital expenditure and data centre investment that offsets typical headwinds from higher borrowing costs. The discussion covers Treasury dynamics, investor positioning, and the need to view US rates developments within a global context.

item.title: From AI ecosystems to industrial strength: The case for US small caps – EN
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · BNPP AM Viewpoint (web) — US small-cap stocks, represented by the Russell 2000, significantly outperformed large-cap companies during the second half of 2025 and first half of 2026, repositioning the asset class as an attractive investment opportunity. The analysis examines factors driving this performance, including exposure to AI ecosystems and industrial strength sectors. This period marks a notable shift in relative valuations and investor positioning toward smaller US equities.

item.title: The Fed Paints itself into a Rate-Hiking Corner
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Market Insights — The Federal Reserve faces a constrained policy position and is expected to raise rates in the coming week despite economic complexity. Understanding the reasoning behind this decision requires examining the contradictory factors influencing Fed policy and their implications for economic growth, interest rates, and investment returns.

item.title: Insights from the OCFO: What It Takes to Build the Agentic Enterprise
item.dc:creator: Jefferies
item.description: Jefferies · Jefferies Insights & Quarterly (web) — Jefferies hosted its fourth annual Office of the CFO Summit in August at the NYSE, convening business leaders from finance, technology, and consulting sectors to discuss building agentic enterprises. The summit explored emerging approaches and technologies that are reshaping corporate finance and operational capabilities.

item.title: Signals & Noise: Four Themes Driving Emerging Markets
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — Emerging markets face headwinds from persistent inflation, potential Fed rate increases, U.S. political uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. Despite these challenges, BofA's David Hauner maintains a constructive view on emerging market carry strategies, identifying four key themes—Treasury developments, Fed policy, U.S. elections, and EM monetary policy—while highlighting attractive opportunities in higher-yielding currencies in Brazil, Colombia, Turkey, and frontier markets, though recommending caution on EM rates and sovereign spreads.

item.title: Sports Investing: Big league opportunities | Wealth Management
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · Deutsche Bank Wealth CIO Insights (web) — Professional sports franchises and related assets are emerging as attractive investment opportunities due to strong brand value, predictable revenue streams, international expansion potential, and ability to raise prices. The sector combines characteristics of real assets with growth dynamics, appealing to institutional investors seeking diversification. Deutsche Bank's wealth management team outlines how sports-related investments fit within portfolio construction strategies.

item.title: Signals & Noise: AI Exposure, Less Volatility? Enter Converts
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — Convertible bonds offer investors a way to gain exposure to the artificial intelligence investment theme with reduced volatility compared to holding common stocks directly. Approximately one-third of the convertible market is now linked to AI-related companies in infrastructure, data centers, and hyperscalers, and these securities provide a combination of equity participation, downside protection, and embedded volatility exposure. Recent market weakness has made convertibles more attractively priced for investors confident in long-term AI growth but concerned about valuations and drawdowns.

item.title: Global Rates & FX Views: CPI, Fed, & buyback implications
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — Bank of America's Economics and Rates Strategy teams analyze the latest CPI data and its implications for Federal Reserve policy, along with developments in U.S. Treasury buybacks. The discussion, featuring multiple analysts, examines key macroeconomic takeaways from the inflation report and market implications.

item.title: VIDEO: Moments in Market History - What can we learn from key landmark events?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · On Investors' Minds — JPMorgan's Market Insights team examines landmark market events from 1929 to the Global Financial Crisis to identify turning points and their underlying causes. The six-part series features Chief Market Strategist Gabriela Santos and Chief Global Strategist David Kelly discussing historical upheavals and lessons for contemporary investors.

item.title: The Macro Brief - Crunch time for US interest rates
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Global Viewpoint — HSBC analysts discuss the critical juncture for US interest rates and analyze the resulting implications across bond markets, equities, and the broader economy. The conversation examines how rate movements could shape financial conditions and investor positioning across multiple asset classes.

item.title: Take Two: ECB raises rates; China launches economic support package – EN
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · BNPP AM Viewpoint (web) — The European Central Bank raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% and revised upward its inflation forecasts for 2027 and 2028, citing Middle East conflict concerns. Concurrently, China launched an economic support package to address domestic economic challenges. These developments reflect divergent policy responses in major economies.

item.title: The Reindustrialization of America Is Underway
item.dc:creator: Apollo
item.description: Apollo · Apollo Insights & Outlook (web) — After four decades of offshoring, the U.S. is experiencing a reindustrialization effort driven by pandemic supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions, and supportive government policies. This shift represents a fundamental change in the economic structure as manufacturing and industrial production move back to American shores.

item.title: Private Equity Co-Investments: A Closer Look at an Evolving Landscape
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GSAM Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs Asset Management analyzes whether private equity co-investments generate value and examines the importance of deal selection in this market. The research explores how co-investment opportunities have evolved and what factors contribute to returns. The analysis provides insights into the potential benefits and risks of this investment approach.

item.title: The Credit Market Lens: One AI Trade for Now, Many Trades Later
item.dc:creator: PIMCO
item.description: PIMCO · PIMCO Insights & Outlooks (web) — PIMCO examines how credit investors should evaluate AI-related investments differently than equity investors, focusing on whether credit spreads provide adequate compensation for the diverse risks associated with financing AI infrastructure buildout. While equity investors concentrate on which companies win the AI race, credit investors must assess broader risks embedded in financing the proliferation of AI technologies. The framework distinguishes between near-term AI financing opportunities and longer-term credit implications.

item.title: Central bank spotlight, and an update on China’s economy
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · PERSPECTIVES Weekly — Central banks including the Federal Reserve, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan are making rate decisions this week, with markets focused on whether recent bond market volatility has altered policy trajectories and central bank confidence in inflation narratives. Economic data from China will also be closely monitored for implications on commodity demand, regional markets, and global companies with significant China exposure.

item.title: US Rates: And you’re not gonna reach my telephone
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan researchers discuss the latest US inflation data and its implications for rates markets. The podcast analyzes recent economic indicators and explores how inflation trends are shaping interest rate expectations and market positioning.

item.title: Global Data Pod Weekender: September song
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — Major central banks including the ECB, Fed, and BoJ implemented rate hikes in September 2026, marking what JPMorgan economists characterize as the beginning of a broad tightening cycle after a period of easing. This represents a significant shift in monetary policy direction across the world's largest economies.

item.title: Why the Middle-Class Squeeze Is Getting Worse
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — A Morgan Stanley economics discussion explores how the American middle class is being squeezed by rising essential costs while wealth divergence creates a K-shaped economy. The analysis examines how factors like inflation in necessities and artificial intelligence development are reshaping household finances and financial security across income levels.

item.title: Mixed Markets, Fed Feels Hike Heat (E276)
item.dc:creator: DoubleLine
item.description: DoubleLine · DoubleLine Minutes — DoubleLine's portfolio managers reviewed market activity during a shortened holiday week in early September, noting mixed performance across asset classes. The discussion covered central bank policy pressures and market reactions to Fed rate trajectory expectations. Trading volumes were lighter due to the holiday calendar.

item.title: Global FX: Post-CPI and pre-Fed FX round up
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan researchers analyze foreign exchange market dynamics following the latest US CPI release and ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision. The discussion evaluates currency resilience across different scenarios, particularly within a potential hiking cycle, and examines the implications for global FX markets.

item.title: Global Rates: Dissecting the sell-off in European rates, next week’s BoE meeting
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan analysts discuss the recent decline in European government bond yields and preview the upcoming Bank of England monetary policy decision scheduled for September 2026. The conversation examines the drivers behind the eurozone rate sell-off and implications for UK policy direction.

item.title: Global Data Pod: The ECB is on the move, will the BoE follow?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — The ECB has taken a hawkish stance on monetary policy, and analysts are examining whether the Bank of England will adopt a similarly hawkish approach in its upcoming decision. The discussion explores the implications of coordinated or divergent central bank actions across major economies.

item.title: The Week Ahead - Crunch time for the Fed and the BOJ
item.dc:creator: Nomura
item.description: Nomura · Nomura — The Week Ahead — Central banks face critical decisions this week as bond markets show vulnerability. The Federal Reserve will address August CPI data and provide guidance, while the BOJ meets alongside important economic data from China and India. European central banks including the ECB and BOE also have significant decisions on tap.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research team provides integrated analysis spanning multiple asset classes including equities, fixed income, commodities, and currencies. The research examines macroeconomic developments and their implications for portfolio positioning across global markets.

item.title: View from the markets: Tightening again – EN
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · BNPP AM Viewpoint (web) — Central banks are resuming rate increases amid geopolitical tensions from the Iran conflict that began in February. The European Central Bank raised rates this week, with markets expecting similar moves from the Federal Reserve and Bank of England. Investors are favoring floating rate debt, high yield bonds, and shorter-duration inflation-linked bonds over longer-term fixed-rate securities in this tightening environment.

item.title: What comes next for European markets?
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Macro Minutes — RBC Capital Markets discusses emerging opportunities in European markets amid ongoing changes and explains how the firm is enhancing its capabilities across people, products, and technology to serve clients more effectively. The episode highlights RBC's European expertise and commitment to delivering solutions that help clients navigate evolving market conditions.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research provides analysis spanning multiple asset classes, including equities, fixed income, currencies, and commodities. The division publishes regular insights, research publications, and video content to inform investment decision-making across global markets.

item.title: Sustainable Funds Beat Traditional Funds in 2026
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · MS Insights (web) — Sustainable funds outperformed traditional funds in the first half of 2026, with the asset class reaching a record $4.24 trillion in total assets despite experiencing only modest inflows during the period.

item.title: 25 Years of Benchmark-Free Investing
item.dc:creator: GMO
item.description: GMO · GMO Research Library & 7-Year Forecast (web) — Ben Inker discusses GMO's 25-year history of benchmark-independent asset allocation, examining how the firm's approach has evolved and the principles that guide investment decisions outside traditional index constraints. He considers how current market conditions may present opportunities for investors willing to deviate from conventional benchmarks.

item.title: The future of treasury: From back office to strategic forefront
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Making Sense — Treasury functions are evolving from operational back-office roles into strategic business drivers that enhance resilience and growth. The discussion examines how technology, real-time data, and AI are transforming treasury operations, along with the evolving skill requirements for treasury leaders seeking to generate competitive advantage through data-driven insights.

item.title: 270: Sports, Markets and Investing: What Separates Skill From Good Luck
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · The Bid — This episode explores parallels between elite sports and investing, examining how small statistical edges compound through repeated decisions and strong processes. The discussion covers hit rates, payoff ratios, teamwork and preparation in both domains, using examples from tennis, soccer and basketball to illustrate decision-making principles applicable to fixed income portfolio management.
